# S260 — Launch prompts: drop well-specified and split, take them from the spec check and a default

*Proposed, and blocked on the owner.* `ork run`, `ork wave start` and the TUI launch stop asking "Well specified?" and "Split?" for every item. Well specified comes from the spec check (an item that starts has passed it), split defaults to no, and `--well-specified` and `--split` stay as optional overrides. This reverses decided adj records 86, 87 and 135 ("no default"), so nothing here is built until the owner decides (Q1).

**Findings:** Owner 2026-11-03: asking well specified and split for every ticked item is friction. Facts: both go only to 'slicer relay-roles recommend' (internal/daemon/runs.go:369). No matrix row sets well_specified today (all 20 rows null in the ork matrix); split picks r4 (split part) against the whole-slice rows. The spec check runs on every launch (friction F7) and checks what rule u4 means by well specified. Proposed: drop both prompts from the TUI composer (internal/tui/waves.go, launch.go) and from ork run and ork wave start; well specified comes from the spec check (Ready means yes), split defaults to no, the flags stay as optional overrides, and --yes stops requiring them. Docs: docs/design.md:1193, docs/dashboard.md:1268, docs/guide.md:237. adj records 86, 87 and 135 say 'no default' for both, so the owner must decide a replacement first (interview before specifying). Related: S116, S167, S258. · **Size:** M · **Tree:**

## Why

Owner, 2026-11-03 (findings): asking well specified and split for every ticked item is friction. The owner is revisiting adj 86 (`run.lineup-inputs`, decided `prompt`: ask at confirmation; `--yes` requires both flags), adj 87 (`run.prompt-answers`, decided `confirm-no`: well specified and split have no default) and adj 135 (`ui.wave-composer`, decided `ask-on-tick`: space ticks a row and asks the two inputs). Those records are decided; this slice proposes to replace them and does not treat that as decided.

What the code at HEAD of main shows (read 2026-11-07 at a1114e2):

- The two answers go only to `slicer relay-roles recommend ID --well-specified yes|no --split yes|no` (`internal/slicercli/write.go:107-109`), called once when the daemon plans a run (`internal/daemon/runs.go:381`). `RunParams.WellSpecified` and `Split` are on the wire (`internal/daemon/runs.go:55`).
- `ork run` takes `--well-specified` and `--split`, requires both with `--yes` (`internal/cli/run.go:52-72`, citing adj 86 and 87) and otherwise asks both (`:104-115`). It plans (`:118-120`), then runs the spec check (`:131-132`).
- `ork wave start` does the same per item (`internal/cli/wave.go:91-105`, `:137-151`), plans every item, then runs the spec check, which holds the items that are not Ready (`:167`).
- The TUI asks both on tick on the Waves screen (`internal/tui/waves.go:300-317`) and in the single launch (`internal/tui/launch.go:23-24`, `:150-170`), then runs the spec check (`launch.go:303`).
- Rule u4 of the matrix says "well specified" means the slice names its files, failing tests, implementation steps and checks, and needs no open owner decision (`slicer relay-roles show`); the spec check checks that and answers Ready or questions per item (`internal/daemon/speccheck.go:43`, `:68`, `:186`).
- No matrix row sets `well_specified` today (findings: all 20 rows null in the ork matrix on 2026-11-03); split picks r4 (split part) against the whole-slice rows.

So the order today is: answers, plan, spec check. An item that is not Ready is held and never starts, so its plan's well-specified answer is not used. An item that starts has passed the spec check, which is the same test as u4.

Open question Q1 (open, 2026-11-07; the owner is revisiting adj 86, 87 and 135):
- (a) Replace: plan every item with well specified = yes and split = no; the spec check holds any item that is not Ready, as today; `--well-specified` and `--split` stay as optional overrides; `--yes` no longer requires them; the TUI asks nothing on tick.
- (b) Defaults only: keep the prompts but give them defaults (well specified = yes, split = no), so Enter accepts both.
- (c) Keep adj 86, 87 and 135 as decided (no change; retire this slice).
Recommendation: (a). The spec check already decides what "well specified" means, and the held list already keeps a not-ready item from starting. Recording the answer is the owner's: a new adj record that supersedes 86, 87 and 135 (`adj ask`, then the owner decides; ork never runs `adj supersede`).

Related: S116 (spec check), S167, S258 (spec check row).

## Implement

1. Do not start until the owner answers Q1 and the answer is recorded in adj. If the answer is (c), stop and report; the slice is retired by the owner.
2. Tests first; see each fail.
3. CLI: remove the asks in `run` and `wave start`; default `well` to yes and `split` to no when the flag is empty; keep the flags' validation; drop the `--yes` requirement and update the comments that cite adj 86 and 87 to cite the new record.
4. TUI: remove the two stages of the single launch and the tick inputs on the Waves screen; plan at once with the defaults.
5. Docs: describe the defaults and the overrides; mark them *proposed* until the adj record is decided. CHANGELOG last.
6. Do not change the wire, the spec check or `slicer relay-roles recommend`.

Owner decisions: 2026-11-07 (interview). Q1: option (a), replace. Plan every item as well specified = yes and split = no; the spec check holds any item that is not Ready; --well-specified and --split stay as optional overrides; --yes no longer requires them; the TUI asks nothing on tick. The owner must record the adj record that supersedes 86, 87 and 135 before this is built (ork never runs adj supersede).
